module_title: Advanced Extensions - Macros, Templates, and Executables
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical exams, this advanced module analyzes the security-focused extensions used for Macro-enabled Office files, structural templates, and core operating system executables.

core_concepts.title: Macro-Enabled Extensions
core_concepts.description:
If an MS Office file contains embedded 'Macros' (automated VBA coding scripts), its extension changes to end with an 'm' (Macro) instead of an 'x' for security reasons.
- Word: `.docm`
- Excel: `.xlsm`
- PowerPoint: `.pptm`
(Because Macros can carry viruses, Windows will throw a security warning before opening these files).

core_concepts.title: Template Extensions
core_concepts.description:
A Template is a pre-formatted, read-only structural blueprint used to repeatedly create similar files (like a standard Resume layout). Their extensions feature a 't' (Template):
- Word Template: `.dotx`
- Excel Template: `.xltx`
- PowerPoint Template: `.potx`

core_concepts.title: Executable Files (.exe)
core_concepts.description: The single most important file type in the Windows operating system. Any file that runs a software program, installs an application, or launches a game carries the `.exe` (Executable) extension.

core_concepts.title: System and Archive Files (.dll and .zip)
core_concepts.description:
- `.dll` (Dynamic Link Library): Core system files in Windows that contain shared code. Multiple different programs can load a single `.dll` file simultaneously to save RAM.
- `.zip` / `.rar`: Compressed Archive files. They bundle multiple large files into one single, highly compressed folder for easy emailing or storage.

important_entities.name: Batch File (.bat)
important_entities.significance: A plain text file containing a series of commands designed to be executed sequentially by the Windows Command Prompt (CMD) to automate routine system tasks.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The x vs. m vs. t Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
In high-level exams, you must distinguish between the final letters of Office extensions:
- Ends in `x`: Standard, safe XML file.
- Ends in `m`: Contains executable Macro code.
- Middle letter `t`: A read-only structural Template.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A Word template file is `.dotx`. Remembering DOT as 'DOcument Template' will instantly help you identify it in a multiple-choice lineup.

exam_strategy_tips: In Tier-2 'Find the odd one out' questions, you may see `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pdf`, and `.exe`. The odd one out is strictly `.exe`, because it is a system program (Application), whereas all the others are data/document files.
